items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A potential-outcome law class with a known uniform design. Fix public parameters \(d\ge1\), \(\alpha,\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\gamma\in[1,3]\), \(L>1/2\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and the interior profile \(x_0=(1/2,\ldots,1/2)\in(0,1)^d\). A primitive law \(P=\mathcal L(X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\) is a Borel probability law on \([0,1]^d\times\{0,1\}^3\) with observed outcome \(Y=(1-A)Y(0)+AY(1)\), observed law \(P_o=\mathcal L_P(X,A,Y)\), treatment-record marginal \(P_{XA}=\mathcal L_P(X,A)\), propensity \(e_P(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)\), arm means \(\mu_{a,P}(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]\) and effect \(\tau_P=\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\), each taken as its continuous representative on the closed cube. For \(s\in(0,3]\) and \(f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R\), the extended-real Hölder norm \(\|f\|_{H^s}\) is the maximum of the sup norms of the partial derivatives \(\partial^\kappa f\), \(|\kappa|\le\lceil s\rceil-1\), and of the \((s-\lceil s\rceil+1)\)-Hölder seminorms in Euclidean distance between arguments \(x\ne x'\) of the derivatives of order \(\lceil s\rceil-1\), and is \(+\infty\) when these continuous derivatives do not exist. The class \(\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\) consists of the laws with \(\mathcal L_P(X)=\mathrm{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), \(A\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X\), \(e_P\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), \(\mu_{0,P},\mu_{1,P}\in[0,1]\), \(\|e_P\|_{H^\alpha}\le L\), \(\|\mu_{0,P}\|_{H^\beta}\le L\) and \(\|\tau_P\|_{H^\gamma}\le L\). The associated public rate quantities are \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(\Delta=2\gamma+d+\gamma d/S\), \(S_{\mathrm{crit}}=\gamma d/(2\gamma+d)\), \(q_*=\gamma d/[S(2\gamma+d)]\), the oracle order \(r_o(n)=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m)=\max\{r_o(n),(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta}\}\) with \(N=n+m\); constants \(c,c_0>0\) and \(C<\infty\) depend only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\) and are quantified separately in each claim. The published comparator model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{KBRW}}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) is the bounded-density Hölder model of the source theorem, under that source's own constants: observed laws whose covariate density is bounded above by a constant and whose propensity, control regression and effect are \(\alpha\)-, \(\beta\)- and \(\gamma\)-smooth. It is descriptive comparator notation and fixes no numerical density cap or radius from the present model.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: The two-channel sampling experiment. With \(n\ge2\) labeled and \(m\ge0\) outcome-free records, total treatment-record count \(N=n+m\), the original-record dataset is \(\mathcal D_{n,m}=((X_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n,(\widetilde X_j,\widetilde A_j)_{j=1}^m)\) with an independent randomizer \(U\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\), and its law under a primitive law \(P\) is \(\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)=P_o^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\otimes\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\). The length-\(N\) treatment-record sequence \(\mathcal D^T=((X_i^T,A_i^T))_{i=1}^N\) concatenates the labeled records with outcomes discarded and the auxiliary records. A randomized decision is a Borel map \(T:(\mathcal D_{n,m},U)\to\mathbb R\) with absolute-loss risk \(\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P)=\int|T-\tau_P(x_0)|\,d\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)\) and minimax risk \(R(n,m)=\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R_{n,m}(T,P)\); a supplied-propensity decision \(T^e\) additionally receives \(e_P\), with oracle risk \(R^e(n,m)\). The sharp rate is \(r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=r_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m)\), attained by the total data-only decision \(T_*\); the pair \((r_*,T_*)\) is the unequal-channel program \(\mathfrak F\). Asymptotic statements run along arbitrary auxiliary-size sequences \((m_n)_{n\ge2}\); for a tolerance \(\zeta\ge1\) the oracle-attainment region is \(\mathcal B_*(\zeta)=\{(n,m):r_*\le\zeta r_o(n)\}\), and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) is a target absolute-error scale.

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl:
The rectangular projection estimator. For a localization input \(0<h\le1/2\) and a grid input \(J\ge1\) with fine-cell side \(\delta=h/J\), let \(C_h=x_0+[-h/2,h/2]^d\), \(d
u_h(x)=w_h(x)\,dx\) with \(w_h(x)=h^{-d}\mathbf1\{x\in C_h\}\), and let \(I\) be the identity on \(L_2(
u_h)\). The coarse vector \(r:C_h	o\mathbb R^q\), \(q= inom{d+2}{2}\), is the scaled Legendre basis of total-degree-at-most-two polynomials, orthonormal under \(
u_h\), with \(r_0=r(x_0)\) and \(p_v=r^	op v\) for \(v\in\mathbb R^q\). The space \(V_J\) of cellwise degree-two polynomials on the equal \(J^d\)-cell half-open partition of \(C_h\) has rank \(k=qJ^d\), cellwise orthonormal basis vector \(\mathbf b_J=(b_{J,1},\ldots,b_{J,k})^	op\), kernel \(K_J(x,x')=\mathbf b_J(x)^	op\mathbf b_J(x')\) and orthogonal projection \(\Pi_Jf(x)=\int K_J(x,x')f(x')\,d
u_h(x')\). The role split uses \(\ell=\lfloor n/2floor\) outcome-role indices \(I_L=\{1,\ldots,\ell\}\) and \(t=N-\ell\) treatment-role indices \(I_T=\{\ell+1,\ldots,N\}\). The outcome-role projection \(\widehat\eta_J^L\), rectangular vector \(\widehat R_{h,J}\), raw and symmetrized matrices \(\widehat Q^{\mathrm{raw}}_{h,J}\), \(\widehat Q_{h,J}\) and population matrix \(Q_{P,h,J}=\mathbb E\widehat Q_{h,J}\) define the clipped, eigenvalue-guarded decision \(\widehat T_{h,J}\); the public tuning \(h_*=	frac12\max\{n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},(nN)^{-1/\Delta}\}\), \(J_*=\lceil h_*^{-\max\{0,\gamma/S-1\}}ceil\) gives \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}=\widehat T_{h_*,J_*}\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: The marked-component lower-bound experiment. For a fine scale \(0<\delta\le h\le1/2\) and amplitudes \(a,b>0\), the program \(\mathfrak C\) produces, for each hypothesis index \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}\), a finite prior \(\varpi_\theta\) on primitive laws and a deterministic contrast \(\tau_\theta:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R\): smooth frames on \(C_h\) whose squared entries partition \(B_h^2\) at scale \(\delta\) carry independent sign pairs \((\lambda_z,\eta_z)\) with \(\Pr_\theta(\lambda_z=u,\eta_z=v)=(1+\theta uv/2)/4\), the propensity is \(1/2+a\sum_z\lambda_z\phi_z\), the arm means are \(1/2+b\sum_z\eta_z\phi_z\mp\tau_\theta/2\) and \(\tau_\theta=-2\theta ab\,B_h^2\). The fixed-size mixtures are \(M_\theta=\int(P_o^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m})\,d\varpi_\theta(P)\), compared in squared Hellinger distance \(H^2(M_{+1},M_{-1})=\int(\sqrt{dM_{+1}/d\xi}-\sqrt{dM_{-1}/d\xi})^2\,d\xi\) with \(\xi=M_{+1}+M_{-1}\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \[\|f\|_{H^s}=\max\left\{\max_{|\kappa|\le\lceil s\rceil-1}\|\partial^\kappa f\|_\infty,\ \max_{|\kappa|=\lceil s\rceil-1}\sup_{x\ne x'}\frac{|\partial^\kappa f(x)-\partial^\kappa f(x')|}{\|x-x'\|_2^{s-\lceil s\rceil+1}}\right\}.\] The value is \(+\infty\) if the indicated continuous derivatives do not exist.

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl:
For public \(L>1/2\) and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and an underlying primitive Borel law \(P=\mathcal L(X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\), membership in \(\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\) is the following existential property of that law:
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)=\bigl\{P:\;&
 \mathcal L_P(X)=\mathrm{Unif}([0,1]^d),\quad
 A\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X,\\
&\exists\text{ Borel }g_e,g_0,g_1:[0,1]^d\to[0,1]
 \text{ such that}\\
&g_e(X)=\mathbb E_P[A\mid X]\quad P\text{-almost surely},\\
&g_0(X)=\mathbb E_P[Y(0)\mid X]\quad P\text{-almost surely},\\
&g_1(X)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)\mid X]\quad P\text{-almost surely},\\
&g_e(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\quad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d),\\
&\|g_e\|_{H^\alpha}\le L,\quad \|g_0\|_{H^\beta}\le L,
 \quad\|g_1-g_0\|_{H^\gamma}\le L,\\
&g_0(x)\in[0,1]\quad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d),\\
&g_1(x)\in[0,1]\quad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d)\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
For each admitted law, the notation \(e_P,\mu_{0,P},\mu_{1,P}\) designates witnesses \(g_e,g_0,g_1\) of this existential condition. The notation \(\tau_P\) designates the canonical continuous representative of the almost-sure conditional causal contrast specified in its symbol definition. The designated witnesses satisfy
\[
 \mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x)
 \qquad(\forall x\in[0,1]^d).
\]
Thus the six witness and contrast predicates above are exactly \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), \(\mathrm{ass:propensity\text{-}holder}\), \(\mathrm{ass:control\text{-}holder}\), \(\mathrm{ass:effect\text{-}holder}\), \(\mathrm{ass:control\text{-}interior}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:treated\text{-}interior}\), with the existing uniform-design and exchangeability predicates. The witness convention neither selects an arbitrary raw conditional version nor adds an estimator-side condition.

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: \[\delta=h/J,\quad K_J(x,x')=\mathbf b_J(x)^\top \mathbf b_J(x'),\quad\Pi_Jf(x)=\int K_J(x,x')f(x')\,d\nu_h(x').\] Weighted basis expressions are zero outside \(C_h\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: \[\mathcal D^T=((X_i^T,A_i^T))_{i=1}^N,\qquad (X_i^T,A_i^T)=\begin{cases}(X_i,A_i),&1\le i\le n,\\(\widetilde X_{i-n},\widetilde A_{i-n}),&n<i\le N.\end{cases}\]\[\ell=\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\quad t=N-\ell,\quad I_L=\{1,\ldots,\ell\},\quad I_T=\{\ell+1,\ldots,N\}.\] Outcome-role records are \((X_j,A_j,Y_j)\) for \(j\in I_L\). Treatment-role records are \((X_i^T,A_i^T)\) for \(i\in I_T\). The latter role retains no outcomes.

items.label: Definition P-8
Definition P-9
items.nl: For the public overlap level \(\varepsilon\), let \(g(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)/2\). Then\[\widehat T_{h,J}=\begin{cases}\mathrm{clip}_{[-1,1]}(r_0^\top\widehat Q_{h,J}^{-1}\widehat R_{h,J}),&\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q_{h,J})\ge g(\varepsilon),\\0,&\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q_{h,J})<g(\varepsilon).\end{cases}\]

items.label: Definition P-12
items.nl:
For the public parameters \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), the construction \(\mathfrak C\) has inputs \((h,\delta,a,b)\), with \(0<\delta\le h\le1/2\) and \(a,b>0\). Define the following fixed real functions:
\[
\chi(u)=\begin{cases}\exp(-1/u),&u>0,\\0,&u\le0,\end{cases}
\qquad
\vartheta(u)=\frac{\pi}{2}\frac{\chi(u)}{\chi(u)+\chi(1-u)},
\]
\[
\omega_z(u)=\begin{cases}
\sin\vartheta(u-z+1),&z-1\le u\le z,\\
\cos\vartheta(u-z),&z\le u\le z+1,\\
0,&u\notin[z-1,z+1],
\end{cases}
\qquad z\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Here \(u\in\mathbb R\). The two formulas at \(u=z\) have the same value. For \(w\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(x\in[0,1]^d\), put
\[
B(w)=\prod_{v=1}^d\frac{\chi(1-4w_v^2)}{\chi(1)},
\qquad B_h(x)=B\bigl((x-x_0)/h\bigr),
\qquad
\psi_{\mathbf z}(x)=\prod_{v=1}^d
  \omega_{z_v}\bigl((x_v-x_{0,v})/\delta\bigr).
\]
The finite index set and frame entries are prescribed by
\[
\mathcal I=\left\{\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^d:
 |z_v|\le1+\frac{h}{2\delta}\ \text{for every }v\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\right\},
\qquad
\phi_{\mathbf z}(x)=B_h(x)\psi_{\mathbf z}(x)
\quad(\mathbf z\in\mathcal I).
\]
For \(\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}\), define
\[
F_\lambda(x)=\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}\lambda_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x),
\qquad
G_\eta(x)=\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}\eta_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}(x).
\]
For \(\theta\in\{-1,+1\}\), let \(\rho_\theta=\theta/2\) and prescribe the product sign-pair weights
\[
w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)=
 \prod_{\mathbf z\in\mathcal I}
 \frac{1+\rho_\theta\lambda_{\mathbf z}\eta_{\mathbf z}}{4}.
\]
Prescribe the Borel functions
\[
e_\lambda(x)=\tfrac12+aF_\lambda(x),
\qquad
\tau_\theta(x)=-4ab\rho_\theta B_h(x)^2,
\]
\[
\mu_{0,\theta,\eta}(x)=\tfrac12+bG_\eta(x)-\tfrac12\tau_\theta(x),
\qquad
\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}(x)=\tfrac12+bG_\eta(x)+\tfrac12\tau_\theta(x).
\]
The probability-valued domain of the construction consists of inputs for which these three Bernoulli success-probability functions take values in \([0,1]\) for every sign array and every cube point. On that domain, \(P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}\) is the primitive Borel law obtained by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \([0,1]^d\), and, given \(X=x\), drawing \(A,Y(0),Y(1)\) independently as Bernoulli variables with the respective success probabilities \(e_\lambda(x),\mu_{0,\theta,\eta}(x),\mu_{1,\theta,\eta}(x)\). These explicitly prescribed functions are the designated conditional-margin witnesses of the constructed law. The deterministic output of \(\mathfrak C\) is the pair of contrasts \(\tau_\theta\) and finite pushforward measures
\[
\varpi_\theta=
 \sum_{\lambda,\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal I}}
 w_\theta(\lambda,\eta)\,
 \operatorname{Dirac}(P_{\theta,\lambda,\eta}),
\qquad \theta\in\{-1,+1\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Dirac}(P)\) denotes the unit point mass at the primitive law \(P\). No choice of frames, weights, compensation, or output remains to be made after the inputs have been fixed. Class membership, probability validity on the theorem's input domain, and the asserted information properties are conclusions to be proved, not clauses of this construction.

items.label: Definition P-13
items.nl: Derive \((r_*,T_*)\) for \(\tau_P(x_0)\) by local polynomial reproduction and unequal-channel projection correction starting from \(\widehat T_{h,J}\). Optimize localization and resolution over public parameters. Match data-only risk with fixed-size common-propensity mixtures from \(\mathfrak C\), analyzing sparse and dense treatment-record occupancy separately.

items.label: Definition P-16
items.nl:
For each original dataset and independent randomizer, define the decision by
\[
 T_*(\mathcal D_{n,m},U)=\widehat T_{h_*,J_*}(\mathcal D_{n,m})
                       =\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}}(\mathcal D_{n,m}),
\]
using exactly the moments, empirical cutoff, clipping, role split, and public tuning in \(\mathrm{def:moments}\), \(\mathrm{def:estimator}\), and \(\mathrm{def:tuning}\). The randomizer is ignored.

items.label: Assumption A-3
items.nl: For the public overlap level \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), the designated Borel propensity witness satisfies \(e_P(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\).

items.label: Assumption A-4
items.nl: The designated Borel propensity witness satisfies \(\|e_P\|_{H^\alpha}\le L\).

items.label: Assumption A-5
items.nl: The designated Borel control-mean witness satisfies \(\|\mu_{0,P}\|_{H^\beta}\le L\).

items.label: Assumption A-6
items.nl: The canonical continuous causal contrast satisfies \(\|\tau_P\|_{H^\gamma}\le L\).

items.label: Assumption A-7
items.nl: The designated Borel control-mean witness satisfies \(\mu_{0,P}(x)\in[0,1]\) for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\).

items.label: Assumption A-8
items.nl: The designated Borel treated-mean witness satisfies \(\mu_{1,P}(x)\in[0,1]\) for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: \[v^\top Q_{P,h,J}v=\int e_P(x)(1-e_P(x))p_v(x)^2d\nu_h(x)+\|(I-\Pi_J)(e_Pp_v)\|_{L_2(\nu_h)}^2\ge\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\|v\|_2^2\] for every \(P\in\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\), \(h\in(0,1/2]\), \(J\ge1\), and \(v\in\mathbb R^q\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl:
For the public bases and projection in \(\mathrm{def:projection}\), there is a constant \(C\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(0<h\le1/2\), and \(J\ge1\), the following conclusions hold. First, writing \(p_*=\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), the degree-\(p_*\) Taylor polynomial \(p\) of \(\tau_P\) at \(x_0\) has a representation \(p=r^\top\vartheta\) with
\[
 \|\tau_P-p\|_{\infty,C_h}\le Ch^\gamma,
 \qquad \|\vartheta\|_2\le C,
 \qquad r_0^\top\vartheta=\tau_P(x_0).
\]
Second,
\[
 \sup_{x\in C_h}\|r(x)\|_2\le C,
 \qquad \sup_{x\in C_h}\int|K_J(x,x')|\,d\nu_h(x')\le C,
 \qquad \iint K_J(x,x')^2\,d\nu_h(x)\,d\nu_h(x')=k.
\]
Finally, for every coordinate \(r_u\) of \(r\),
\[
 \|(I-\Pi_J)(e_Pr_u)\|_{L_2(\nu_h)}\le C\delta^\alpha,
 \qquad
 \|(I-\Pi_J)\mu_{0,P}\|_{L_2(\nu_h)}\le C\delta^\beta.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
Write \(\bar R=\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}\widehat R_{h,J}\). Under \(\mathrm{ass:sample\text{-}law}\), for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(n\ge2,m\ge0,0<h\le1/2,J\ge1\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}\|\widehat R_{h,J}-\bar R\|_2^2
 +\mathbb E_{\mathsf E_{n,m}(P)}\|\widehat Q_{h,J}-Q_{P,h,J}\|_F^2
 \le C\left\{\frac1{nh^d}+\frac{k}{nNh^{2d}}\right\}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
For any two probability laws \(\mathbb B,\mathbb C\), write
\[
 \mathsf h^2(\mathbb B,\mathbb C)
   =\int\left(\sqrt{d\mathbb B/d\xi}-\sqrt{d\mathbb C/d\xi}\right)^2d\xi,
 \qquad \xi=\mathbb B+\mathbb C.
\]
For finitely many pairs of probability laws on their respective common spaces,
\[
 \mathsf h^2\left(\bigotimes_{u_*}\mathbb B_{u_*},
                 \bigotimes_{u_*}\mathbb C_{u_*}\right)
 \le\sum_{u_*}\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B_{u_*},\mathbb C_{u_*}).
\]
If two joint laws have the same marginal \(\nu\) for a coordinate \(z\), and conditional laws \(\mathbb B_z,\mathbb C_z\) with measurable densities, then their squared Hellinger distance is
\(\int\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B_z,\mathbb C_z)d\nu(z)\).
Appending a common independent probability law leaves squared Hellinger distance unchanged. These formulas use the same normalization as \(\mathrm{def:hellinger}\).

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
Let \((\mathbb B_z)\) and \((\mathbb C_z)\) be two families of probability laws on one measurable observation space, with a common prior \(\omega\) on their index set, and let \(v_0\ge1\) be an integer. Let \(\Psi\) be a real-valued functional on a model containing both families. Define squared Hellinger distance by \(\mathsf h^2(\mathbb B,\mathbb C)=\int(\sqrt{d\mathbb B/d\xi}-\sqrt{d\mathbb C/d\xi})^2d\xi\), where \(\xi=\mathbb B+\mathbb C\). If, for some \(s_0>0\) and \(0\le u_0<2\),
\[
 \Psi(\mathbb B_z)-\Psi(\mathbb C_{z'})\ge s_0\quad\hbox{for all }z,z',
 \qquad
 \mathsf h^2\left(\int\mathbb B_z^{\otimes v_0}d\omega(z),
                  \int\mathbb C_z^{\otimes v_0}d\omega(z)\right)\le u_0,
\]
then every measurable decision \(\widehat\Psi\) has supremum expected absolute loss over that model at least
\[
 \frac{s_0}{4}\left\{1-\sqrt{u_0(1-u_0/4)}\right\}.
\]
This is the absolute-loss specialization of Lemma 1 in Section 3 of \cite{KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024}.

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
For fixed public \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), if \(S<S_{\mathrm{crit}}\), there is \(c>0\) such that for every \(n\ge2,m\ge0\) with \(n\le N=n+m\le n^{q_*}\),
\[
 R(n,m)\ge c(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta}.
\]
This is a lower bound on the original-record risk, including every Borel decision using the independent randomizer.

items.label: Lemma lem:published-cate-benchmark
items.nl:
Put \(s_{\mathrm{pub}}=(\alpha+\beta)/2\). The two numerical exponents and the smoothness cutoff displayed in Section 3, Theorem 1, of \cite{KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024} obey
\[
 \frac{1}{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s_{\mathrm{pub}})}
   =\frac{2\gamma}{2\gamma+d+\gamma d/(\alpha+\beta)},
 \qquad
 \frac{1}{2+d/\gamma}=\frac{\gamma}{2\gamma+d},
\]
\[
 s_{\mathrm{pub}}<\frac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \alpha+\beta<\frac{\gamma d}{2\gamma+d}.
\]
For every public \(n\ge2\), their numerical piecewise expression is therefore
\[
 \begin{cases}
 n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s_{\mathrm{pub}}))},
       &s_{\mathrm{pub}}<(d/4)/(1+d/(2\gamma)),\\
 n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},
       &s_{\mathrm{pub}}\ge(d/4)/(1+d/(2\gamma))
 \end{cases}
 =\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 n^{-2\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\gamma d/(\alpha+\beta))}\right\}.
\]
These are exactly the supervised numerical branches at \(m=0\), including equality at the cutoff. The claim is an exponent-and-cutoff comparison only.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: Use \(\mathcal D^T\) from \(\mathrm{def:roles}\): its records indexed by \(I_T\) form the treatment role, independently of labeled records indexed by \(I_L\) in the outcome role. For every fixed public \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\) with \(L>1/2\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), there exists \(C<\infty\), depending only on these parameters, such that, simultaneously for all \(n\ge2,m\ge0,h\in(0,1/2],J\ge1\),\[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)}\mathcal R_{n,m}(\widehat T_{h,J},P)\le C\min\{1,h^\gamma+\delta^S+(nh^d)^{-1/2}+(nNh^d\delta^d)^{-1/2}\}.\] The decision is finite and Borel on every dataset, clips to \([-1,1]\), and uses Gram guard \(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)/2\). Its public tuning satisfies\[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)}\mathcal R_{n,m}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{up}},P)\le Cr_{\mathrm{up}}(n,m).\]

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: For every fixed public \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\) with \(L>1/2\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), there are constants depending only on these parameters such that\[\exists\,0<c\le C<\infty\quad\forall n\ge2,\ m\ge0:\quad c\,r_o(n)\le R^e(n,m)\le C\,r_o(n).\] The upper bound is attained by degree-two local polynomial smoothing under the known uniform design at bandwidth \(n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)}\) of \(A_iY_i/e_P(X_i)-(1-A_i)Y_i/(1-e_P(X_i))\), with output bounded by one. The lower bound holds on the same-class subfamily \(e_P=\mu_{0,P}=1/2\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: For every fixed public \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\) with \(L>1/2\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), constants may depend only on these parameters. Unconditional corollary of the sharp frontier: let \(r_*\) be the established directly evaluable rate in \(\mathrm{thm:sharp\text{-}annotation\text{-}frontier}\), including every imbalance branch. For every sequence \((m_n)\),\[\frac{R(n,m_n)}{R^e(n,m_n)}=O(1)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r_*(n,m_n;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=O(r_o(n)),\]\[\frac{R(n,m_n)}{R(n,0)}\longrightarrow0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\frac{r_*(n,m_n;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)}{r_*(n,0;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)}\longrightarrow0.\] The first equivalence is eventual membership in \(\mathcal B_*(\zeta)\) for some finite \(\zeta\). The sharp frontier establishes \(r_*=r_{\mathrm{up}}\) as the numerical rate and \(R(n,m)\asymp r_*\) uniformly in \(n,m\). Its explicit branches are\[R(n,m)\asymp\begin{cases}r_o(n),&S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}},\ \ N\ge n,\\(nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta},&S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\ \ n\le N\le n^{q_*},\\r_o(n),&S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\ \ N\ge n^{q_*}.\end{cases}\] Oracle attainment is equivalent to \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}(n+m_n)/n^{q_*}>0\). For \(S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}}\) it holds for every auxiliary-size sequence, including \(m_n=0\). For \(S<S_{\mathrm{crit}}\), \(q_*>1\): bounded \(m_n/n\) leaves the supervised order; \(n\ll n+m_n\ll n^{q_*}\) gives the pair-information branch; total counts of order \(n^{q_*}\) or larger give the oracle order. Equality of the two rate branches is included. Moreover,\[\frac{R(n,m_n)}{R(n,0)}\longrightarrow0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S<S_{\mathrm{crit}}\ \text{and}\ m_n/n\longrightarrow\infty.\] The supervised reduction is\[R(n,0)\asymp\begin{cases}n^{-2\gamma/\Delta},&S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\\r_o(n),&S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}}.\end{cases}\] Substitution of \(s_{\mathrm{pub}}=(\alpha+\beta)/2\) into the numerical formula in KBRW Theorem 1 makes its exponents and smoothness split coincide algebraically with these supervised branches, including equality, as recorded in \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}cate\text{-}benchmark}\). This is a descriptive comparison under the source theorem's own bounded-density model and constants. It asserts no exact fixed-radius or density-cap slice and no minimax transfer. The published lower bound does not descend by restriction to the present known-uniform class; its lower bound is instead established by the original uniform-design converse in \(\mathrm{thm:sharp\text{-}annotation\text{-}frontier}\). The public domain \(\beta\in(0,1],\gamma\in[1,3]\) contains no \(\gamma<\beta\) parameters. Finally, achieving worst-case absolute-error order \(\varepsilon\) is equivalent, up to class-dependent constants, to\[n\gtrsim\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma)},\qquad n(n+m)\gtrsim\varepsilon^{-(2+d/\gamma+d/S)},\qquad n+m\ge n.\] The rate-level acquisition region is \(\{(n,m):r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\le\varepsilon\}\); its necessary and sufficient sample-growth conditions follow from all the established branches above.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
The directly evaluable rate and total data-only decision are given in \(\mathrm{def:sharp\text{-}rate}\) and \(\mathrm{def:sharp\text{-}decision}\). For every fixed public \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\) with \(L>1/2\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), there are \(0<c\le C<\infty\) depending only on these parameters, such that, simultaneously for all \(n\ge2,m\ge0\),
\[
 c\,r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)
 \le R(n,m)
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)}\mathcal R_{n,m}(T_*,P)
 \le C\,r_*(n,m;d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma).
\]
The lower bound covers every randomized original-record Borel decision. With \(N=n+m\), all branches, including equality, are
\[
 r_*=
 \begin{cases}
 r_o(n),&S\ge S_{\mathrm{crit}},\quad N\ge n,\\
 (nN)^{-\gamma/\Delta},&S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\quad n\le N\le n^{q_*},\\
 r_o(n),&S<S_{\mathrm{crit}},\quad N\ge n^{q_*}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The two formulas coincide at \(N=n^{q_*}\); there is no additional imbalance branch or equality logarithm in this primitive class.

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
Fix the public parameters \(d\ge1\), \(\alpha,\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\gamma\in[1,3]\), \(L>1/2\), and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\) of \(\mathcal M(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\). There exist \(c\in(0,1]\), \(c_0>0\), and \(C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\varepsilon)\), with the following property. For every \(n\ge2\), \(m\ge0\), and
\[
0<\delta\le h\le\tfrac12,\qquad
0<a\le c\delta^\alpha,\qquad
0<b\le c\delta^\beta,\qquad
ab\le ch^\gamma,\qquad
N\delta^d\le c_0,\qquad N=n+m,
\]
the prescribed output \((\varpi_\theta,\tau_\theta)_{\theta\in\{-1,+1\}}\) of \(\mathfrak C\) consists of finite priors supported on \(\mathcal M\) and deterministic contrasts, and satisfies
\[
\tau_P=\tau_\theta\quad(P\in\operatorname{supp}\varpi_\theta),\qquad
\tau_\theta(x_0)=-2\theta ab,\qquad
H^2(M_{+1},M_{-1})\le CnNh^d\delta^da^2b^2.
\]
In particular, the target separation is \(4ab\ge cab\). The entire designated propensity function \(e_P\) has the same distribution under the two priors. Consequently, for every integer \(k_{\mathrm{aux}}\ge0\),
\[
\int P_{XA}^{\otimes k_{\mathrm{aux}}}\,d\varpi_{+1}(P)
=
\int P_{XA}^{\otimes k_{\mathrm{aux}}}\,d\varpi_{-1}(P).
\]
This equality also holds conditionally on every collection of auxiliary covariates, using the explicit conditional kernels of the construction. Every singleton labeled mixture has conditional law uniform on \(\{0,1\}^2\). Conditional on all \(N\) covariates, form the graph whose vertices are the records in \(C_h\), joining two vertices when their maximum-norm covariate distance is at most \(2\delta\). The conditional mixed laws factor across its connected components. Auxiliary-only components and singleton labeled components have identical conditional laws under both hypotheses. The displayed information bound holds uniformly in \(m/n\).
